items.title: Everyone Is All In on the Airbus A321XLR — Except Delta
items.summary: More airlines are embracing long-haul flying on narrowbody jets — in a competitive transatlantic market, they allow airlines to launch service in smaller cities. However, Delta is not convinced.

items.title: How Wellness Hospitality Is Breaking Out of the Luxury Bubble
items.summary: Health-conscious travel is entering the mainstream. Novotel’s Longevity Everyday model shows how hotel brands can extend wellness beyond premium retreats by embedding supportive choices into the ordinary rhythms of a stay.

items.title: Flagship Group Makes First Three Acquisitions For Experiences Roll-Up
items.summary: Appetite for an experiences roll-up has long existed, but Covid put plans on ice. Now P&Ls have had a chance to rebound, and the timing is perhaps even better today, with experiences positioned as a counter-AI play.

items.title: Vrbo’s Biggest Product Push Yet, and What Hosts Need to Know
items.summary: On this episode of Good Morning Hospitality, Michael Goldin, Brandy Canaley, and Jamie Lane sit down with Tim Rosolio, VP of Vacation Rental Partnerships at Expedia Group, to unpack what the expansion says about Vrbo’s strategy for the vacation rental market.

items.title: EU Ends Border ‘Safety Valve’ as Airlines Warn of More Delays

items.title: Flyadeal CEO Reveals Plans for Premium Economy and Long-Haul Network
items.summary: Flyadeal’s move into connecting flights and premium economy marks a natural next step for a budget carrier scaling into long-haul.

items.title: Air India’s New CEO Gets a Clear Mandate: Safety, Reliability and Profit
items.summary: New CEO Tewolde Gebremariam is taking over a very different Air India from the one Campbell Wilson inherited in 2022. The airline has more aircraft, more resources and bigger ambitions, not to forget, much higher expectations.
